[Date]

Aetna Appeals Department  
[Appeal address shown on the denial notice or EOB]

Re: Expedited/standard pre-service appeal of denial  
Member: Morgan Ellison  
Member ID: W176862845  
Reference number: POC-5FADD4BBDE-47544  
Requested service: Total hip replacement  
CPT: 27130  
Date of denial notice: August 14, 2026  
Surgeon: Okafor, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

Dear Aetna Appeals Reviewer:

I appeal Aetna’s denial of the requested total hip replacement. The denial states that the submitted imaging did not support medical necessity. The clinical record, including the May 31, 2026 weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph, demonstrates advanced structural disease and significant functional impairment.

Aetna’s publicly available Hip Arthroplasty Clinical Policy Bulletin, CPB 0287, states:

“Member has advanced joint disease demonstrated by: Pain and functional disability that interferes with activities of daily living (ADLs) from injury due to osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, avascular necrosis, or post-traumatic arthritis of the hip joint; and Limited range of motion (ROM), antalgic gait, and pain in hip joint with passive ROM on physical examination: and Radiographic evidence of either of the following: Avascular necrosis (osteonecrosis) with stage II or III disease; or Moderate/severe osteoarthritis or rheumatoid arthritis of the hip joint (Tonnis grade 2 or 3; see Appendix for Tonnis grading scale).”

The submitted records address these requirements as follows:

- Imaging: The May 31, 2026 weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph shows joint-space narrowing to 1 mm superolaterally, subchondral sclerosis, and osteophytes. These are objective radiographic findings of advanced degenerative joint disease and support moderate-to-severe hip osteoarthritis. Please have the reviewing clinician evaluate the actual radiograph and report rather than relying on a generalized description that the imaging is insufficient.
- Pain and functional disability: Morgan has had 12 months of progressive hip pain that is not relieved by rest. Morgan ambulates with a cane, is limited to one block, and cannot put on shoes without assistance. These limitations interfere substantially with activities of daily living.
- Physical examination: Examination documents range of motion limited by pain and positive provocative testing on the affected side. The cane-dependent, one-block ambulation also documents gait-related functional impairment.
- Conservative treatment: Morgan used NSAIDs for four months without adequate relief. Morgan also completed 20 supervised physical-therapy visits focused on hip-abductor strengthening and gait from April 21, 2026, through June 30, 2026, documented in the physical-therapy discharge note. A corticosteroid injection on April 21, 2026 produced only three weeks of partial relief.

CPB 0287 also states:

“History of unsuccessful conservative therapy (non-surgical medical management; 12 or 24 weeks depending on age/BMI) that is clearly addressed in the medical record with at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consisting of formal physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy) in the past year.”

The record documents prolonged NSAID treatment, a failed injection, and 10 weeks of supervised physical therapy with 20 completed visits. Morgan’s BMI is 29, with no documented relative contraindication requiring 24 weeks of treatment. If Aetna believes that the record must contain additional conservative-treatment documentation, please identify precisely what is missing and allow submission of any additional records or treating-surgeon explanation required under the applicable criteria.

There is no documented active infection, untreated substance-use condition, or other clinical circumstance identified in the submitted summary that would make the requested procedure inappropriate. Morgan is a nonsmoker and has a BMI of 29.

I request that Aetna overturn the denial and authorize CPT 27130. At minimum, please obtain review by an orthopedic physician or other appropriately qualified clinical reviewer who evaluates the actual May 31, 2026 radiograph together with the documented symptoms, examination findings, functional limitations, and treatment history.

If Aetna continues to deny authorization, please provide:

1. The specific imaging finding that Aetna contends is absent or inadequate;
2. The radiographic classification Aetna applied, including the Tonnis grade if that classification was used;
3. The exact CPB 0287 version or other clinical-review criteria applied to this request, including its effective date;
4. The clinical rationale explaining why the documented 1 mm superolateral joint space, subchondral sclerosis, and osteophytes do not satisfy the applicable imaging criteria; and
5. Copies of all documents and clinical records relied upon in making the determination.

Please reverse the denial and approve the requested total hip replacement.

Sincerely,

Morgan Ellison  
[Mailing address]  
[Telephone number]  
[Email address, if desired]

- May 31, 2026 weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph and report  
- Physical-therapy discharge note
